claims.text: Refractory alloying elements have a strong positive mixing enthalpy with Cu.
Equilibrium processing of the RHEA/Cu composite leads to phase inhomogeneity.
A data-driven process-optimization model can identify non-equilibrium processing windows for RHEA/Cu synthesis.
The identified processing windows enable rapid reaction synthesis of RHEA/Cu composites.
The identified processing windows yield a homogeneous and stable RHEA/Cu microstructure despite positive mixing enthalpy.
Machine learning can be used to select and control heating rates, cooling rates, dwell times, and applied pressures during synthesis.
Nuclear-reactor materials must tolerate high temperatures and irradiation-related extreme conditions.
The proposed large-scale processing itself should be performed under irradiation-like conditions.
Non-equilibrium processing rapidly forms an interfacial reaction layer in the RHEA/Cu composite.
The interfacial reaction layer mitigates the positive mixing-enthalpy barrier between the refractory constituents and Cu.
Rapid non-equilibrium processing kinetically bypasses the equilibrium mixing barrier.
The optimized processing conditions promote grain refinement.
The optimized processing conditions promote heterogeneous nucleation that stabilizes the composite against phase separation.
The optimized process produces a fine and homogeneous RHEA/Cu microstructure.
The optimized composite has superior mechanical strength relative to conventionally processed composites.
The optimized composite has superior thermal stability and irradiation resistance relative to conventionally processed composites.
Traditional sintering or alloying typically produces inhomogeneous phases and unstable RHEA/Cu microstructures because of equilibrium mixing limitations.
Scale-up uncertainty and variability in training data may limit the effectiveness of the optimized process.
